attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The head lines give each of the two «(; - 307)» and the body states the year of the beheading, so a `death` is proposed for both. The line enumerates its two members, so Alphaeus gets a folder of his own and the two relate each other, on `docs/CORPUS.md` §10.1. The page: Zacchaeus was deacon of the Church of Gadeira — which the page glosses as a small island of Spain in the Atlantic very close to the Spanish mainland — dragged in chains to the idolaters' tribunal, confessed Christ with courage, was tortured hard and thrown into prison, set for four days and nights on a special instrument of torture; then Alphaeus, full of the Holy Spirit, was brought to the tribunal, his sides were torn, his wounds burnt, and he was thrown into the same prison as his fellow contestant; the next day both were beheaded. No `locations`, the Gadeira of the page being a gloss this reader would not place on a map. No hymn. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

death.note: Two sources four years apart and the interval is widened to hold both, neither narrowed. saint.gr gave the 307 this folder held flat; days.pravoslavie.ru closes the line for 18 ноября ст. ст. with «(303)» and closes its life page «(+ 303)». That page puts the persecution in the reign of Diocletian, «(284–305)», which holds the 303 and not the 307, and this corpus narrows no source’s own reading on that account. Neither page gives a year of birth.
